<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Syrian Civil War]]
**[[Iraqi Air Force]] [[F-16]] jets attack an [[Islamic State group|Islamic State]] explosives factory and other positions inside [[Syria]] near the city of [[Hajin]] in coordination with the [[Syrian Armed Forces]]. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/mideast-crisis-iraq-syria/update-2-iraqi-warplanes-attack-islamic-state-positions-in-syria-idUKL8N1RW3YN (Reuters)] 
*[[War in Donbas (2014–2022)|War in Donbass]]
**[[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] ecology minister [[Ostap Semerak]] warns of a major [[Nuclear accident|nuclear disaster]] if pro-[[Russia]] [[Separatist forces of the war in Donbass|separatists]] go forward with a plan to flood a mine where a small [[nuclear weapon]] was tested in the 1970s. Semerak appeals for international assistance to prevent the flooding. [https://www.irishtimes.com/news/world/europe/ukraine-fears-second-chernobyl-if-militants-flood-nuclear-bomb-mine-1.3467275 (''The Irish Times'')]
*[[Mohammed Haydar Zammar]], a recruiter for the [[September 11 attacks]], is arrested in [[Syria]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/suspected-9-11-recruiter-mohammed-haydar-zammar-captured-syria-report-n867376 (NBC News)]

;Arts and culture
*Prosecutors in [[Minnesota]] say nobody will be charged over the death of [[Prince (musician)|Prince]], who accidentally overdosed on counterfeit [[fentanyl]] pills. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-43829545 (BBC News)]
*[[Independence Day (Israel)|Yom Ha'atzmaut]]
**[[Israel]] celebrates the 70th anniversary of its existence as a Jewish state. [http://www.cbc.ca/news/world/israel-70th-anniversary-1.4626719 (CBC)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[Shoreham Airshow crash]]
**Jet pilot Andy Hill, accused of eleven counts of manslaughter over a 2015 crash at [[Shoreham Airshow]] in [[England]], makes an initial [[Magistrates' court (England and Wales)|Magistrates' Court]] appearance. He indicates he will deny the charges and the case is transferred to [[Crown Court]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-43820847 (BBC News)]
**[[Mount Kirishima]] in [[Kyushu]], [[Japan]], erupts. It is the first time it has erupted since [[1768]]. [http://clicklancashire.com/2018/04/19/volcano-erupts-in-kyushu.html (Click Lancashire)]
*[[Southwest Airlines Flight 1380]]
**The [[United States]] [[National Transportation Safety Board]] declares [[metal fatigue]] caused a fan blade failure that killed a passenger on April 16, the same issue behind [[Southwest Airlines Flight 3472|a similar accident]] on another [[Southwest Airlines]] [[Boeing 737]] in 2016. The [[Federal Aviation Administration]] announces mandatory ultrasonic inspections on fan blades fitted to [[CFM International CFM56#CFM56-7B "Evolution"|CFM56-7B]] engines of which around 8,000 are flying worldwide. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-43818752 (BBC News)]
*[[Indonesia]]'s [[National Transportation Safety Committee]] releases a preliminary report detailing the circumstances of a collision between two passenger planes on a runway at [[Kuala Namu International Airport]] last year. [http://avherald.com/h?article=4accb6aa&opt=0 (The Aviation Herald)]

;International relations
*[[North Korea–South Korea relations]]
**[[South Korea]] states that [[North Korea]] has expressed a desire to denuclearize the [[Korean Peninsula]] without attaching preconditions such as withdrawing US troops. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/apr/19/north-korea-wants-complete-denuclearisation-says-seoul (''The Guardian'')]

;Law and crime
*[[Murder in English law#Causation and foreseeability|Murder in English law]]
**A woman goes on trial in [[England and Wales|England]] accused of murdering a man who was [[assisted suicide|voluntarily euthanised]] in [[Belgium]] after she allegedly attacked him with acid. Prosecutors say medical evidence indicates "he could not bear to live in that condition." [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-bristol-43823752 (BBC News)]
*The High Court in [[Glasgow]] jails corrupt juror Catherine Leahy for six years in the first case of its kind in [[Scotland]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2018/apr/19/juror-jailed-six-years-accepting-bribe-scotland (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Terrorism in Norway]]
**The police bomb group moved out to an apartment in Rosenhoff, Oslo, when informed that there might be explosives in the apartment. One person was found slightly injured. [https://www.aftenposten.no/osloby/i/7lggo4/Bombegruppen-undersoker-mistenkelig-gjenstand-fra-Oslo-leilighet-Det-er-grunn-til-a-ta-det-rolig (''Aftenposten'')]
*Two deputies are shot dead at a Chinese restaurant in [[Trenton, Florida]], in what appears to be a targeted killing. The gunman was found dead outside the restaurant. [https://edition.cnn.com/2018/04/19/us/florida-gilchrist-county-deputies-killed/index.html (CNN)]
*A court in [[Tajikistan]] sentenced a 71-year old woman to 12 years in prison after having links to the [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|Islamic State]] group. [https://eurasianet.org/s/tajikistan-court-jails-71-year-old-over-islamic-state-links (EurasiaNet)]
*A [[United States|US]] federal judge rules the [[US Department of Defense|Department of Defence]] cannot transfer an unidentified [[ISIL|ISIS]] suspect with US-[[Saudi Arabia|Saudi]] [[dual citizenship]] to an unnamed foreign country. [https://edition.cnn.com/2018/04/19/politics/isis-citizen-transfer/index.html (CNN)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Cuban parliamentary election, 2018]]
**[[Miguel Díaz-Canel]] is named the new President of [[Cuba]]. It is the first time in six decades that a Castro family member is not leading Cuba. [http://wtkr.com/2018/04/19/miguel-diaz-canel-named-cubas-new-president/ (WTKR)]
*[[History of Swaziland]]
**Marking the country's 50th anniversary of independence, [[List of monarchs of Swaziland|Swaziland's King]] [[Mswati III]] officially renames the country the [[Kingdom of eSwatini]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-africa-43821512 (BBC News)]
*[[Donald Trump presidential campaign, 2020]]
**Republican Senators [[Ron Johnson (Wisconsin politician)|Ron Johnson]] and [[Bob Corker]] opt not to commit to endorsing [[Donald Trump]] in the 2020 elections. [http://abcnews.go.com/Politics/gop-senators-commit-endorsing-trump-2020/story?id=54583046 (ABC News)]
**[[South Carolina]] senator [[Lindsey Graham]] states that he will [[List of Donald Trump presidential campaign endorsements, 2020|support]] Trump in the 2020 elections. [https://www.postandcourier.com/politics/lindsey-graham-on-trump-s-presidential-bid-i-intend-to/article_82e28d4c-43e8-11e8-80c5-6705797c556d.html (''The Post and Courier'')]
*[[Political appointments of the first Trump administration|Political appointments by Donald Trump]]
**The U.S. Senate votes 50–49 to confirm [[Jim Bridenstine]] as [[List of Administrators and Deputy Administrators of NASA|administrator]] of [[NASA]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trumps-controversial-nasa-chief-narrowly-confirmed/ (CBS News)]

;Sports
* [[2018 NFL season]]
** As expected, the regular-season schedule for the [[2018 NFL season#Regular season|2018 NFL season]] is released, with the [[Super Bowl LII|defending]] champions [[Philadelphia Eagles]] [[Lincoln Financial Field|hosting]] the [[Atlanta Falcons]] in the league's season opener on September 6. [https://sports.yahoo.com/2018-nfl-schedule-eagles-falcons-kick-things-off-full-slate-announced-000936048.html (Yahoo! Sports)]
